title: OTTO-CHARGE ARM
frame: Arm base frame: origin on J1 axis at the mount collar top, +Y up, +Z toward the car, X along the car. Zero pose (all joints 0).

subsystems.name: Riser and mount
subsystems.function: A short steel riser on the cross-slide carries the arm. Its J1 axis is 550 mm above the deck.
how: 4 screws M16 hold the riser to the cross-slide saddle.
8 screws M12 hold the mount plate to the riser.
The arm's power and network cables come up through the riser and J1's hollow shaft.

subsystems.name: Rail, carriage and cross-slide
subsystems.function: Moves the arm's base to where the car's charge inlet is: along the car on a floor rail, and toward the car on a cross-slide.
how: 2 steel beams on the slab carry 2 profile rails and a rack, along the car.
A carriage rides the rails on 4 blocks. A servo gearmotor under it turns a pinion on the rack.
On the carriage 2 rails and a ball screw carry the saddle toward the car and back.
For an inlet on the car's side the base stops beside it, at the same distance from every car.
For an inlet in the rear bumper the base goes past the tail and in behind the car's corner.
The power and coolant lines run in a cable chain in a covered channel in the slab, under the carriage.
The bed is set toward the tail end of the stall. A stall that faces the other way has the same bed, set the other way.

specs.along the car: 1.3 m toward the nose, 2.5 m toward the tail
specs.rails: size 25 along the car, size 20 across
specs.drive: rack and pinion module 3 along, ball screw 20 x 5 across

subsystems.name: J1 base yaw
subsystems.function: Turns the whole arm about the vertical axis to face the charge port.
how: A size 40 actuator in the riser top turns the turret.
Range is +/- 180 degrees. Cables pass through the hollow shaft.

subsystems.name: J2 shoulder pitch
subsystems.function: Leans the upper arm toward or away from the car. It carries the highest load of any joint.
how: A size 50 actuator in the turret boss drives the upper arm.
A nitrogen gas spring balancer carries most of the gravity load, so the gear and brake see less.

subsystems.name: Upper arm
subsystems.function: The 1.344 m cast link from the shoulder to the elbow.
how: A hollow aluminium casting, 7 mm wall.
Its cheek bolts to the J2 output. Its boss clamps the J3 actuator.

subsystems.name: J3 elbow pitch
subsystems.function: Folds the forearm to set the reach and the height of the wrist.
how: A size 40 actuator in the upper arm boss drives the forearm.

subsystems.name: Forearm
subsystems.function: The 1.142 m cast link from the elbow to the wrist centre.
how: A hollow aluminium casting. Its top socket holds the J4 actuator.

subsystems.name: Spherical wrist (J4, J5, J6)
subsystems.function: Points the connector along the port axis. The 3 wrist axes meet at one point, so position and angle solve apart.
how: J4 rolls the forearm end (size 25).
J5 pitches the wrist (size 25).
J6 rolls the tool (size 20). Its output is the tool flange (ISO 9409-1).

subsystems.name: Connector head
subsystems.function: Carries 2 connectors, CCS1 and NACS. It finds the inlet, brings forward the connector the car takes, plugs in, latches, and lets go.
how: A 6-axis force and torque sensor reads the insertion force.
A compliance unit lets the head float up to 6 mm and 3 degrees. A small error cannot jam it.
Stereo cameras and a time-of-flight sensor find the inlet. A light ring helps at night.
Each connector rides a plunge cylinder. The one the car takes comes forward 90 mm. The other stays back, clear of the car.
A solenoid latch locks the connector in the inlet for the charge.

specs.connectors: CCS1 (SAE J1772 combo) and NACS (SAE J3400), liquid-cooled
specs.spacing: 100 mm each side of the tool axis

subsystems.name: Power path in the arm
subsystems.function: Carries the charge current, the coolant and the tool's lines to the connector inside the arm, and power and network to the joints.
how: The charge current comes from the cabinet under the pad to the cable chain, and up the riser in 2 cables.
In each hollow link 2 copper bars carry it, one a pole. Nothing live is in the open.
At the base, the shoulder and the elbow a booted link of braided copper joins 2 terminal boxes. It bends as the joint turns.
From the forearm one last booted link, 1.2 m long, runs to the connector across the wrist.
The coolant for the connector's contacts, the tool's cable and its air line run with the bars and through each boot.
The joints' 10 mm power and network cable runs inside the arm, through the hollow shafts of J1 to J5.

specs.bars: 2 x 40 x 10 mm copper in each link, insulated
specs.flex links: 4, braided copper 400 mm2 a pole, in a silicone boot OD 60 mm, 0.9 to 1.2 m
specs.bend radius: 80 mm moved (the tightest in the twin's 20 poses is 100 mm)
specs.cooling: liquid at the connector's contacts, 2 tubes 8 mm

subsystems.name: Safety and status
subsystems.function: Stops the arm when a person comes near and shows its state to the site.
how: A safety laser scanner on the riser watches the stall at knee height.
An emergency stop on the riser cuts motor power (safe torque off).
Light rings on J2 and the wrist show the state: teal ready, amber moving, green charging, red fault.
